definitions.gloss: completion of a course, finishing a program
definitions.explanation: Successfully completing all requirements of an academic course, training program, or curriculum. Distinct from graduation ({卒業|そつぎょう}), which applies to completing an entire degree program.

examples.japanese: {研修|けんしゅう}を{修了|しゅうりょう}した。
{修了|しゅうりょう}{証書|しょうしょ}が{発行|はっこう}される。
examples.english: A certificate of completion will be issued.

examples.japanese: {大学院|だいがくいん}の{博士|はかせ}{課程|かてい}を{修了|しゅうりょう}するには、{論文|ろんぶん}の{審査|しんさ}に{合格|ごうかく}しなければならない。
examples.english: To complete a doctoral program, you must pass the dissertation review.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{課程|かてい}を{修了|しゅうりょう}する (complete a curriculum)
・{研修|けんしゅう}を{修了|しゅうりょう}する (complete training)
・{修了|しゅうりょう}{証書|しょうしょ} (certificate of completion)
・{修了|しゅうりょう}{式|しき} (completion ceremony)
・{修了|しゅうりょう}{要件|ようけん} (completion requirements)

COMPARISON WITH {終了|しゅうりょう}:
Both are read しゅうりょう but have different meanings:
・{修了|しゅうりょう}: completing a course of study (the {修} kanji means "to study/master")
・{終了|しゅうりょう}: ending or finishing (general sense — the {終} kanji means "to end")

In academic contexts, {修了|しゅうりょう} is used for completing a course or program (especially graduate school), while {卒業|そつぎょう} is for graduating from a school.
